body:
Correction after instrumenting the failure: Model preservation is not involved, and the first paragraph above describes the wrong mechanism.

I ran the api-cache-query E2E pattern (3 parallel Playwright workers, cold `node_modules/.vite`) with every page's HMR WebSocket frames logged. In the failing run:

- Vite discovered `@effect/platform-browser, clsx, effect/http, effect/persistence, parse5` late and broadcast `full-reload`.
- One page had already connected its HMR socket. It received the reload, booted fresh (`foldkit:request-model` answered with no Model), and loaded.
- The other two pages connected their sockets just after the broadcast and never received it. Their module requests had already hit `504 (Outdated Optimize Dep)`, so the entry never executed. Their `body` stayed empty, and they never sent `foldkit:request-model`.

A standalone script that opened the same three pages slightly earlier saw all three receive the reload, and every page loaded. So the hang depends on when each page's HMR socket connects relative to the optimizer's reload, which is why single tabs usually recover and CI retries hide it.

Apps scaffolded with create-foldkit-app (foldkit from npm) did not trigger a forced reload on a cold cache. The late discovery looks specific to the monorepo examples, which alias `foldkit/*` to source while the plugin sets `optimizeDeps.exclude: ['foldkit']`. I have not verified that the exclusion is what stops the scanner from crawling those imports.

Possible directions: pre-include the discovered deps in the examples' shared Vite config (`optimizeDeps.include`), or have the E2E harness warm the dev server and wait for optimization before starting workers.
